description: We are building an advanced health monitoring system for astronauts to track vitals and ensure safety during long-duration space missions. We bring solid foundational skills in science, logic, and basic coding, driven by a deep fascination with space tech and bio-medical engineering.
summary:
Project 0day is an autonomous crew health monitoring and clinical decision support system (CDSS) built for deep space missions like Artemis and crewed Mars transit, where communication latency makes real-time Earth medical support impossible.
Developed as a 100% offline Progressive Web App (PWA), 0day ingests continuous bio-telemetry from wearable smart garments alongside habitat atmospheric and cosmic radiation data. It addresses the challenge of isolated space healthcare by running local edge processing to detect physiological anomalies and instantly deliver step-by-step diagnostic workflows and countermeasure protocols directly to astronaut mission tablets and heads-up displays. 0day is vital because it ensures astronaut medical self-sufficiency, cognitive clarity, and crew safety during critical signal blackouts, while laying a groundwork for autonomous telemedicine in extreme, isolated environments on Earth.
details:
Project 0day is an autonomous crew health monitoring and clinical decision support system (CDSS) engineered for long-duration deep space missions. It continuously ingests live bio-telemetry (heart rate, respiration,Spo2, blood pressure, and core temperature) streamed from wearable smart garments like Astroskin. Operating entirely on local edge processing without needing Ground Control, 0day applies diagnostic algorithms to detect physiological anomalies in real time. When an issue is detected, the system immediately presents step-by-step clinical decision workflows, triage recommendations, and countermeasure protocols directly to the crew through an offline-first Progressive Web App (PWA) interface designed for mission tablets and Heads-Up Displays (HUDs).
Zero-Latency Autonomy: Eliminates reliance on Earth-based medical guidance, overcoming deep-space communication delays (5–20+ minutes) and blackout periods.

Early Anomaly Detection: Identifies subtle cardiac stress, hypoxia, or fatigue trends before they escalate into acute medical emergencies.

Reduced Cognitive Load: Synthesizes raw biological and environmental data into clear visual triage alerts and step-by-step procedures during high-stress scenarios.

Integrated Environmental Context: Cross-references astronaut vital signs with real-time habitat metrics, such as cosmic radiation spikes and atmospheric composition.
The primary impact of 0day is enabling self-sufficient human space exploration beyond Low Earth Orbit (LEO), ensuring astronaut health and mission success when real-time Earth support is impossible. Beyond spaceflight, 0day provides a scalable framework for autonomous telemedicine in extreme, isolated terrestrial environments—such as Antarctic research stations, submarine operations, and remote disaster relief zones.
Frontend & UX: React, Next.js, and Tailwind CSS configured as an offline-first Progressive Web App (PWA) for cross-platform deployment on tablets and HUDs.

Backend & Analytics: JavaScript/TypeScript for client-side data streaming, anomaly evaluation logic, and clinical workflow state management.

Deployment & Hosting: Vercel (`https://0day-nasaapp.vercel.app/`).

Integrations & Simulation:Smart garment telemetry integration models (Astroskin bio-monitor data structures) and simulated environmental sensor streams (radiation/habitat atmospheric sensors).
Multimodal Health & Environment Fusion: Rather than treating vital signs in isolation, 0day dynamically correlates crew biometrics with habitat environmental hazards (e.g., solar radiation events) to generate an integrated Crew Readiness Index.

Zero-Trust Connectivity Design: Built from the ground up around a 100% offline PWA architecture, treating internet connectivity as a luxury rather than an operational requirement.

EVA/Emergency-First UX: Employs high-contrast visual hierarchies tailored for emergency Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) and low-light cabin conditions to ensure readability under physical strain.

Communication Latency & Signal Blackouts: Designing for complete operational isolation during solar flare events or orbital blockages.

Astronaut Stress & Cognitive Fatigue: Keeping user workflows minimalist to prevent decision paralysis during high-stress medical incidents.

Radiation-Hardened Hardware Constraints:Keeping computational overhead lightweight so the algorithms run efficiently on onboard, radiation-shielded space hardware.
